q: Electrolysis is the process whereby _____ is used to bring about a chemical change.
e: Electrolysis is the process whereby electrical energy is used to bring about a chemical change. Electrolysis uses electrical energy to force a non-spontaneous chemical change. Electrical energy is the word this version is asking about.

q: In a conductor, electric current can flow freely, but in a non-conductor (an insulator) it _____.
e: In a conductor, electric current can flow freely, but in a non-conductor (an insulator) it cannot. An insulator, or non-conductor, does not let electric current flow freely. Cannot is the word this version is asking about.

q: All metals either in the solid state or _____ state are conductors.
e: All metals either in the solid state or liquid state are conductors. All metals either in the solid state or.

q: The non-metallic solid, _____ is a conductor.
e: The non-metallic solid, graphite is a conductor. Graphite is the non-metallic solid that conducts because its delocalised electrons can move. Graphite is the unusual non-metallic solid that still conducts electricity.

q: Solid substances such as wood, plastic and rubber do not conduct electricity and they are _____.
e: Solid substances such as wood, plastic and rubber do not conduct electricity and they are non-conductors or insulators. Wood, plastic and rubber are insulators. they do not provide mobile electrons or ions.

q: Semiconductors are substances which have an ability to conduct between conductors and _____.
e: Semiconductors are substances which have an ability to conduct between conductors and non-conductors. A semiconductor conducts between a metal and an insulator. silicon and germanium are the usual examples. Non-conductors is the word this version is asking about.

q: Examples of semiconductors include elemental silicon, germanium, tin, selenium and _____.
e: Examples of semiconductors include elemental silicon, germanium, tin, selenium and gallium arsenide. A semiconductor conducts between a metal and an insulator. silicon and germanium are the usual examples. Silicon is a semiconductor, sitting between a metal conductor and an insulator.

q: Electrolytes are substances that ionise in solution or in a _____ state and can conduct electricity.
e: Electrolytes are substances that ionise in solution or in a molten state and can conduct electricity. Metals conduct in the solid or molten state because they have mobile electrons. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current.

q: Most electrolytes are _____ compounds such as salt solutions.
e: Most electrolytes are ionic compounds such as salt solutions. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current. Ionic is the word this version is asking about.

q: Strong acid and strong base solutions are _____ electrolytes.
e: Strong acid and strong base solutions are strong electrolytes. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current.

q: Weak acid and weak base solutions are _____ electrolytes.
e: Weak acid and weak base solutions are weak electrolytes. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current.

q: Non-electrolytes do not dissociate into ions in solution and cannot conduct _____.
e: Non-electrolytes do not dissociate into ions in solution and cannot conduct electricity. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current. Electricity is the word this version is asking about.

q: Non-electrolytes are _____ compounds such as sugar solution.
e: Non-electrolytes are covalent compounds such as sugar solution. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: Electrodes are usually made of unreactive metals such as platinum or non-metal _____.
e: Electrodes are usually made of unreactive metals such as platinum or non-metal carbon(graphite). Electrodes are often platinum or graphite so the electrode itself does not react. Electrodes are the conductors where oxidation and reduction happen during electrolysis. Graphite is the non-metallic solid that conducts because its delocalised electrons can move.

q: The _____ attracts the positively charged ions (cations).
e: The cathode attracts the positively charged ions (cations). The cathode is the electrode where reduction occurs.

q: The _____ attracts negatively charged ions (anions).
e: The anode attracts negatively charged ions (anions). The anode is the electrode where oxidation occurs.

q: The _____ reaction takes place at the cathode.
e: The reduction reaction takes place at the cathode. The cathode is the electrode where reduction occurs.

q: The _____ reaction takes place at the anode.
e: The oxidation reaction takes place at the anode. The anode is the electrode where oxidation occurs.

q: Electrical conductivity is a fundamental property of a material that quantifies how strongly it conducts _____.
e: Electrical conductivity is a fundamental property of a material that quantifies how strongly it conducts electric current. Fundamental property of a material that quantifies how.

q: Ionic substances do not conduct electricity when they are in solid state because the movement of _____ is restricted.
e: Ionic substances do not conduct electricity when they are in solid state because the movement of ions is restricted. This is because the movement of ions is restricted. Ions is the word this version is asking about.

q: Ionic substances can only conduct electricity in _____ state or in aqueous solutions.
e: Ionic substances can only conduct electricity in molten state or in aqueous solutions. Metals conduct in the solid or molten state because they have mobile electrons. In the molten state ionic compounds have mobile ions, so they conduct and can be electrolysed.

q: Metals contain free _____ electrons.
e: Metals contain free valence electrons. Metals contain free electrons in this chemistry fact.

q: According to Arrhenius' Ionic Theory, electrolytes contain electrically charged particles called _____.
e: According to Arrhenius' Ionic Theory, electrolytes contain electrically charged particles called ions. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current.

q: An electrochemical cell is a device that converts chemical energy into electrical energy or vice versa when a chemical reaction occurs by _____.
e: An electrochemical cell is a device that converts chemical energy into electrical energy or vice versa when a chemical reaction occurs by electrical energy. An electrochemical cell converts chemical energy to electrical energy, or the reverse in electrolysis. Electrical energy is the word this version is asking about.

q: There are two fundamental types of electrochemical cells: electrolytic cell and _____ cell.
e: There are two fundamental types of electrochemical cells: electrolytic cell and chemical cell. An electrochemical cell converts chemical energy to electrical energy, or the reverse in electrolysis. Chemical is the word this version is asking about.

q: A _____ is a negative electrode and donates electrons.
e: A cathode is a negative electrode and donates electrons. Electrodes are the conductors where oxidation and reduction happen during electrolysis. The cathode is the electrode where reduction occurs.

q: A _____ is a positive electrode and accepts electrons.
e: A anode is a positive electrode and accepts electrons. Electrodes are the conductors where oxidation and reduction happen during electrolysis. The anode is the electrode where oxidation occurs.
